Hi Olivia — thanks for flagging this and for the CSV. I've looped in Lauren from Billing Ops and David from the metering team so they can look at the tombstone attribution and the raw token rows you requested.

Quick note from me: "tombstoned session" is our internal label when a long-lived session KV cache was compacted/expired and subsequent cleanup logic re-attributed residual KV tokens to the originating session window. That can surface as retroactive tokens in a short window. Lauren/David — can you validate whether this matches Edulogic's invoice lines and share the explanation + sample rows?

Ben

Hi Olivia — we dug into your export and see the 12,072-token block that Ben referenced. Below is a concise breakdown: 

- What happened: A housekeeping job triggered on Nov 5 that finalized several long-running sessions. When those sessions were tombstoned (their KV cache compacted), our post-process merged small orphaned KV prefixes back into the last active window for attribution. That process is correct behaviour, but it can look like a retroactive token charge.

- Why you saw it now: The tombstone job finalizes at commit time; if the session had intermittent traffic across Oct 30–Nov 4, the attribution can land on Nov 5/6 accounting buckets. In your export, the rows with the tag "tombstone_reattrib" are the ones that moved.

- Rounding/partial-token heuristics: We count fractional tokens produced during internal aggregation; these are summed then rounded at the invoice line level. The 12,072 number includes 84 fractional tokens that rounded up due to the per-request aggregation window.

Requested next steps from us:
1) I'll attach a sanitized sample of the re-attributed rows (see attachment usage_window_export_EDG-4791.csv).
2) If you'd like, we can issue a pro-rata credit for the tombstone re-attribution while you reconcile.

Could you confirm the HubSpot account ID and whether you want us to proceed with a provisional credit while you validate the rows?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Billing Operations Lead
Redwood Inference

Olivia — following up with the sample rows you asked for. Below are three sanitized lines pulled from our metering store (all timestamps in UTC):

id: edg-4791-session-9934, window_start: 2026-11-03T22:15:00Z, window_end: 2026-11-03T22:16:30Z, type: request, tokens: 42.7, tag: normal
id: edg-4791-session-9934, window_start: 2026-11-04T03:02:00Z, window_end: 2026-11-04T03:02:05Z, type: request, tokens: 7.3, tag: normal
id: edg-4791-session-9934, window_start: 2026-11-05T00:00:00Z, window_end: 2026-11-05T00:00:00Z, type: tombstone_reattrib, tokens: 12.0, tag: tombstone_reattrib

Notes:
- The "tokens" field in our raw store keeps fractional values. Aggregation sums fractional tokens across windows then rounds at the invoice line.
- The tombstone_reattrib line is a synthetic attribution we insert during cleanup; it represents merged prefixes (small residuals) and not a new user-initiated request.

Proposed resolution: We recommend a one-time adjustment: credit the tombstone_reattrib tokens for customer accounts where the net effect is >1% of monthly usage. For Edulogic, that produces a credit of 11.23 USD on your November invoice. We can issue that credit now if you confirm.

I can also export the detailed per-request rows (redacted) if you want a full reconciliation.

-David
